chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Abu Saeed al-Madainy, who said:

I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and said to him, 'May I be your ransom, can I go to the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him)?' He said, 'Yes, O Abu Saeed! Go to the grave of the son of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), the most fragrant of the fragrant, the purest of the pure, and the most righteous of the righteous. So when you visit him, Allah will write for you, because of it, twenty-five Hajjs.'

key_terms.أَبَرِّ الْأَبْرَارِ: The most righteous of the righteous
key_terms.أَطْيَبِ الطَّيِّبِينَ: The most fragrant of the fragrant
key_terms.ابْنِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: Son of the Messenger of Allah

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for visiting the grave of Imam al-Husayn (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Abu Sa'id al-Madani receives from Imam al-Sadiq (as) the specific title 'Ibn Rasul Allah' (Son of the Messenger of Allah) for Imam al-Husayn, emphasizing his unique lineage and status as the pinnacle of righteousness. The promise of twenty-five Hajjs underscores the immense spiritual weight of Ziyarah in Shia tradition, linking physical pilgrimage to the grave with the ritual pilgrimage to Mecca. This hadith serves as a foundational text for the devotional practice of visiting the shrine, reinforcing the concept of *Ziyarat* as a means of drawing closer to God through the Ahl al-Bayt.
